title: From Gujarat to Hollywood: Himesh Patel Shines in Nolan's Record-Breaking The Odyssey
excerpt: The British-Indian actor, born to Gujarati parents in Cambridgeshire, plays Odysseus' right-hand man Eurylochus in the $264 million opening weekend blockbuster — his second collaboration with Christopher Nolan.
body:
• Himesh Patel, a British-Indian actor born to Gujarati parents in Cambridgeshire, plays Eurylochus — Odysseus' second-in-command — in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey.
  • The film opened to $264.1 million worldwide, making it the biggest global debut in Nolan's career.
  • This is Patel's second Nolan collaboration after Tenet, and Screen Rant ranked his performance among the film's top five.
  • Patel next stars as a lead in Ryan Coogler's The X-Files reboot.

Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey stormed theaters this weekend with a record-breaking $264.1 million global opening — $124.5 million domestically and $139.6 million internationally — making it the biggest worldwide debut of the director's career, according to Reuters. Among the film's stacked ensemble of Academy Award winners and A-list stars, one name stands out for the Indian diaspora: Himesh Patel, the British-Indian actor who plays Eurylochus, Odysseus' trusted lieutenant and right-hand man throughout Homer's epic voyage.

Who Is Himesh Patel

Himesh Jitendra Patel was born in 1990 in Cambridgeshire, England, to parents who emigrated from Gujarat, India. His family ran a newsagent shop, and even after landing his first major acting role, Patel continued delivering newspapers for the family business — a detail he has spoken about with characteristic self-deprecation.

His breakthrough came at age 17 when he was cast as Tamwar Masood in the BBC soap opera EastEnders, a role he held for nine years from 2007 to 2016. That marathon run on one of Britain's most-watched shows gave Patel both craft and visibility, but it was Danny Boyle's 2019 musical comedy Yesterday — in which he played Jack Malik, a struggling musician who wakes up in a world where The Beatles never existed — that launched him internationally.

"A generation of South Asian actors — Dev Patel, Riz Ahmed, Kumail Nanjiani, Mindy Kaling — have moved from niche roles to leading major studio productions."

Since then, Patel has built a filmography that signals serious range: Adam McKay's satire Don't Look Up alongside Leonardo DiCaprio and Meryl Streep, the Channel 4 sitcom Damned, and most notably the HBO miniseries Station Eleven (2021), for which he earned a Primetime Emmy nomination for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Limited Series.

His Role in The Odyssey

In The Odyssey, Patel plays Eurylochus, a veteran of the Trojan War who serves as Odysseus' second-in-command on the perilous journey home. It is a substantially larger role than the marketing suggested — Screen Rant counted 16 scenes, placing him third in screen time behind Matt Damon (Odysseus) and Tom Holland (Telemachus).

Screen Rant ranked Patel's performance among the film's top five, writing: "It takes a unique kind of actor to stand toe-to-toe with Academy Award winner Matt Damon delivering one of the best performances of his career, but Patel does exactly that." Critics noted how Patel navigates Eurylochus' arc from loyal ally to uneasy detractor with seamless precision, at times "single-handedly conveying the stakes and horrors of Odysseus' voyage home."

This marks Patel's second collaboration with Nolan, following his role in the 2020 sci-fi thriller Tenet. Speaking to The Playlist about working with Nolan, Patel said: "He has a way of creating an intimacy even in the biggest of environments."

The Growing Indian Presence in Hollywood

Patel's casting in what is now 2026's biggest live-action opening reflects a broader shift in Hollywood. A generation of South Asian actors — Dev Patel, Riz Ahmed, Kumail Nanjiani, Mindy Kaling — have moved from niche roles to leading major studio productions. Dev Patel headlined Monkey Man, his directorial debut, last year. Ahmed won an Oscar for Sound of Metal. Nanjiani leads Marvel's Eternals franchise.

What sets Himesh Patel apart is the quiet steadiness of his ascent. He did not arrive in Hollywood through a splashy Bollywood crossover or a viral moment. He spent a decade grinding on a British soap, then let the work speak — transitioning from television to prestige television to working repeatedly with one of cinema's most selective directors. For British Indians and the broader Gujarati diaspora, his trajectory from a Cambridgeshire newsagent to the third-most prominent role in a $264 million Nolan blockbuster is a potent marker of what is now possible.

What's Next for Patel

Patel is next set to star as one of the lead characters in Ryan Coogler's highly anticipated The X-Files reboot, further cementing his place in Hollywood's top tier. At 36, with two Nolan films, an Emmy nomination, and a growing list of collaborations with elite filmmakers, Himesh Patel is no longer an actor to watch — he is one who has decisively arrived.
